title: Learning as wealth
literal_meaning: Learning is a great treasure; children, acquire it.
explanation: The verse calls learning wealth and directly addresses children. Unlike a possession handed over once, learning must be acquired through effort. The comparison gives everyday study a value beyond an immediate reward; it does not promise that education alone removes every hardship.
meaning_odia: ଏଠାରେ ବିଦ୍ୟାକୁ ବଡ଼ ଧନ ବୋଲି କହି ପିଲାମାନଙ୍କୁ ତାହା ଅର୍ଜନ କରିବାକୁ ଡକାଯାଇଛି। ପଢ଼ିବା, ପଚାରିବା ଓ ଶିଖିବାରେ ଲାଗୁଥିବା ପରିଶ୍ରମକୁ ଏହି ତୁଳନା ମୂଲ୍ୟ ଦିଏ। ଏହା ଶିକ୍ଷାର ମହତ୍ତ୍ୱ ବୁଝାଏ; ପଢ଼ିଲେ ଜୀବନର ସବୁ ଅସୁବିଧା ଦୂର ହେବ ବୋଲି ନିଶ୍ଚୟତା ଦିଏନାହିଁ।
usage_example: A grandparent encourages a child to spend a little time learning something new each day, even when there is no examination ahead. (Original imagined occasion.)
cultural_context: The direct address to children and paired lines make this a didactic verse. The captured compilation places it under instructive Dhaga but supplies no author or literary work; attribution must remain unresolved.
odia_summary: ବିଦ୍ୟାକୁ ମହାଧନ କହି ପିଲାମାନଙ୍କୁ ଶିଖିବା ପାଇଁ ଉତ୍ସାହ ଦିଆଯାଇଛି।
english_summary: Calling learning a treasure gives the effort of acquiring knowledge an enduring value.
odia:
